title: Regular rational toric models of completed log charts
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine saturated sharp commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let $k$ be any field of characteristic zero, and let $n\geq0$. Sharp means that $0$ is the only unit. Write $k[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the finite-sum monoid polynomial ring, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, and let
$$A=B_k(P,n)=\left(k[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]\right)^\wedge_{(z^p\ (p\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)}$$
be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The ring $A$ is a reduced Noetherian excellent local ring [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], and its natural monomial map
$$\mathbf Q[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]\longrightarrow A$$
is regular, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres. With the log structures associated to $P\to\mathbf Q[P][t]$ and $P\to A$, the corresponding scheme morphism is strict and both log schemes are fs log regular [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. In particular these maps, and finite disjoint unions of them, are morphisms to which a regular-functorial characteristic-zero resolution algorithm applies. The case $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$ is included; no finite-generation hypothesis on $k/\mathbf Q$ is imposed.

source.place: VI 1.6(i), printed p.70, and VIII proof of Theorem 3.4.15, third paragraph, printed p.114 (the regular rational toric model and complete qe input) No Stacks tag states this combined result; the cited place is in the archived ILO volume.

proof.text: Put $R_F=F[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for $F=\mathbf Q,k$, $\mathfrak m=(z^p\ (p\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset R_k$, and $L=(R_k)_{\mathfrak m}$. The displayed ideal is maximal since $R_k/\mathfrak m=k$. Finite generators of $P$ together with the $t_i$ generate $R_F$ as an $F$-algebra. Hence [lem-exc-fields-excellent] and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] make $R_{\mathbf Q},R_k,L$ excellent. To identify the completion of $L$ with $A$, take $s\notin\mathfrak m$. Its residue is a nonzero scalar $c\in k$ and $s=c+u$, $u\in\mathfrak m$. Modulo $\mathfrak m^j$, its inverse is $c^{-1}\sum_{a=0}^{j-1}(-u/c)^a$. Thus $R_k/\mathfrak m^j\to L/(\mathfrak mL)^j$ is an isomorphism for every $j$, compatibly with transition maps; their inverse limits identify $\widehat L=A$ with the same monomial map.

source.place: Tags 07QW (proposition-ubiquity-excellent, fields) and 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent); the completion identification is the written finite geometric-series argument.

proof.text: The monoid $T=P\oplus\mathbf N^n$ is fs and sharp by checking finite generation, cancellation, saturation and units componentwise. Its monoid algebra $k[T]$ is $R_k$, and its nonconstant monomial ideal is $\mathfrak m$. The field $k$ is a complete regular Noetherian local ring: [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] gives regularity and its zero maximal ideal has constant quotient system $k$. Apply [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension] with $D=k$ and monoid $T$. It gives that $A$ is a Noetherian local integral domain, hence reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $A$ is complete for $\mathfrak mA$. The same dimension node gives $A/\mathfrak mA=k$, so $\mathfrak mA$ is its maximal ideal. Now [lem-per-complete-local-excellence] makes $A$ excellent.

source.place: VI 1.6(i), p.70, completed monoid model; excellence is Stacks 07QW (proposition-ubiquity-excellent, complete local rings).

proof.text: The coefficient map $\mathbf Q\to k$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. Its only fibre is $k$. In characteristic zero every finite purely inseparable extension of $\mathbf Q$ is trivial by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; therefore [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] makes this fibre geometrically regular. Thus $\mathbf Q\to k$ is regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] along the finite-type map $\mathbf Q\to R_{\mathbf Q}$. The monomial-basis identification $k\otimes_{\mathbf Q}R_{\mathbf Q}\cong R_k$, $c\otimes z^pt^e\mapsto cz^pt^e$, identifies its base change with $R_{\mathbf Q}\to R_k$. This use of finite-type base change assumes finite generation of $R_{\mathbf Q}/\mathbf Q$, already proved in step 1, and imposes none on $k/\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Tags 07BZ (definition-regular) and 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change); characteristic-zero purely inseparable convention: fields.tex Tag 09HE.

proof.text: The localization $R_k\to L$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. At a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R_k$ its fibre is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ if $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and is the zero ring otherwise: localizing the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ either inverts only nonzero elements or inverts zero. These fibres are geometrically regular, since any field extension of the first fibre is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring], while the zero ring has no prime local rings. Hence $R_k\to L$ is regular. Since $L$ is excellent, it is a G-ring by [def-exc-excellent-ring], and the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] at its maximal prime gives the regular map $L\to\widehat L=A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] to the chain $R_{\mathbf Q}\to R_k\to L\to A$, using step 3. At each application its fibre-Noetherianity hypothesis holds: a fibre of a map to a Noetherian ring $C$ is a quotient of a localization of $C$; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (for the quotient map) give Noetherianity. The targets $R_k,L,A$ are Noetherian by steps 1--2. We have proved the asserted regularity of $R_{\mathbf Q}\to A$.

source.place: Tags 07BZ (definition-regular), 07GH (definition-G-ring) and 07QI (lemma-regular-composition); localization flatness: algebra.tex Tag 00HT.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathbf Q}$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with the associated $P$-chart log structures. They are fs by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The chart-compatible monomial map defines a log morphism $f:X\to Y$. It is strict: the pullback log structure is the logification of the same composite $P\to R_{\mathbf Q}\to A$. Indeed, for any log structure $K$ on $X$, both this pullback and the associated $P$-chart represent compatible maps $P\to K(X)$ with this structural map. The universal property in [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening] identifies them, with identity on $P$ and on units. This proves strictness, rather than assuming it from regularity.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69, associated-chart conventions; VIII proof of Theorem 3.4.15, p.114, the obvious strict morphism to the rational monoid polynomial model.

proof.text: Give $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ the trivial log structure. It is log regular, since its nonunit log ideal and characteristic rank are zero and the field is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. Taking the face $\{0\}$ of the sharp monoid $P$, [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] gives that $P^{\rm gp}$ is finite free. For $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$, use the compatible charts $0\to P$. The group map is injective with torsion-free cokernel $P^{\rm gp}$. The comparison scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[P]$, and the comparison map is the polynomial projection $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[P]$, smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], using the affine-locally smooth-ring-map characterization in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The hypotheses of [lem-per-log-smooth-invertible-torsion-log-regular] hold (torsion subgroup has order one). It follows that $Y$ is log regular.

source.place: VI 1.5(ii) and 1.8, p.70, toric log regularity and log-smooth preservation; polynomial smoothness: Stacks algebra.tex Tags 00T6 and 00T7.

proof.text:
We check the defining log-regularity criterion at a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ over $\bar y$ of $Y$. Both schemes are Noetherian excellent: use steps 1--2 and [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] with their single affine covers. By [lem-per-regular-strict-local-model], the map of strict local rings $C=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}\to B=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ is regular. Strictness from step 5 identifies their characteristic monoids and identifies the nonunit log ideal of $B$ with $IB$, where $I\subset C$ is that of $Y$. Explicitly its stalk logification is $M_{Y,\bar y}\oplus_{C^\times}B^\times$; a local ring map reflects units, so the same monoid elements are nonunits, with their structural images extended to $B$. Put $r=\operatorname{rank}\overline M_{Y,\bar y}^{\rm gp}$ and $E=B/\mathfrak m_CB$. The cited strict-local-model node, applied to the closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$, gives a regular map $C/I\to B/IB$ with closed fibre $E$. Since $C/I$ is regular by step 6, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-map-ascent] makes $B/IB$ regular. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the two flat local maps $C\to B$ and $C/I\to B/IB$. Their common closed fibre gives
$$\dim B=\dim C+\dim E=\dim(C/I)+r+\dim E=\dim(B/IB)+r.$$
This is precisely [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]'s criterion for log regularity of $X$ at $\bar x$. No finite-presentation assertion about the completion morphism is used.

source.place: VI 1.2, p.69, stratum and dimension criterion; agent expansion for this strict regular map, using Stacks Tags 031E and 00ON through the cited ascent and height-formula nodes.

proof.text: The domain property of $A$ already makes $X$ reduced. Log regularity of $Y$ and [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] make its local rings normal domains, hence reduced. Both $X,Y$ are excellent by steps 1--2 and the affine-cover lemma used in step 7; in particular they are quasi-excellent. They are schemes over $\mathbf Q$, and step 4 proves that $f$ is regular. Thus they satisfy the input and morphism hypotheses of [lem-per-qe-ordinary-regular-resolution]. For a finite disjoint union use the finitely many affine component covers: they give Noetherian quasi-excellent reduced rational schemes, and each fibre and each local map of the union morphism is a fibre or local map of one component. Hence the union morphism is regular and the same resolution node applies. The empty union is covered by its explicit empty-input clause.

source.place: VIII Theorem 2.3.10, pp.91--93, and proof of Theorem 3.4.15, p.114; VI 1.4 and VIII 3.4.1, normality of fs log regular schemes.

proof.text: If $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$, then $R_{\mathbf Q}=\mathbf Q$, $R_k=L=A=k$, $\mathfrak m=0$, and both log structures are trivial. Step 3 is exactly regularity of $\mathbf Q\to k$; all subsequent constructions reduce to these same maps. The componentwise argument for $P\oplus\mathbf N^n$ also covers just $P=0$ or just $n=0$. No step restricts the transcendence degree or algebraic degree of $k/\mathbf Q$.
